summary: Bildudalur Airport (BIU/BIBD) is a small regional airport serving the village of Bildudalur in Iceland's remote Westfjords (Vestfirðir) peninsula. It provides a vital air link connecting one of Iceland's most isolated regions to Reykjavík, with scheduled domestic flights operated primarily by Icelandair. The airport sits along scenic fjord country, making it a gateway for travelers exploring the dramatic landscapes of the Westfjords.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly to Bildudalur Airport?
A: Icelandair (formerly Air Iceland) operates scheduled domestic flights connecting Bildudalur to Reykjavík. Flights are typically limited to one or two daily rotations.

Q: How far is the airport from Bildudalur village?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers outside the village of Bildudalur, with a short drive of approximately 5 minutes by car.

Q: Are there car rentals available at the airport?
A: Rental car services are generally limited at this small regional airport, so it is advisable to pre-arrange a vehicle or coordinate transport in advance with local providers.

Q: When is the best time to fly to the Westfjords?
A: Summer months (June to August) offer the most reliable weather, longest daylight hours, and accessible mountain roads, though flights operate year-round subject to weather conditions.
transport_tips: Pre-arrange a rental car or taxi in advance, as on-site ground transport options are very limited. The drive into Bildudalur village is short but roads in the surrounding Westfjords can be challenging, so plan extra time if heading further into the peninsula. In winter, check weather conditions closely as flights to BIU are frequently affected by strong winds and low visibility common to the Westfjords.
local_tip: If you're visiting in summer, ask at the airport about combining your flight with a boat tour from Bildudalur harbor to the spectacular Látrabjarg cliffs, Europe's westernmost point and a famous puffin-watching site.
